newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Workers threaten general strike in Honduras.
newsitem.headline: Workers threaten general strike in Honduras.

text.p: Honduras' leading labour unions on Thursday threatened a general strike as the government struggled to end a public sector workers' stoppage and stem growing labour unrest.
Leaders from the country's three largest labour unions met with government officials to negotiate on workers' demands that the government tame public sector price hikes and raise wages.

"If we do not receive a satisfactory answer from the government, we plan to launch a general strike," Efrain Aguilar, vice president of the Honduras Unitary Confederation of Workers (CUTH), told reporters.
In mounting labour unrest, 7,000 workers marched in three cities on Wednesday to demand higher wages and 14,000 hospital workers went on strike, treating only the seriously ill.

The government of President Caros Roberto Reina, 70, has faced unrest and strikes by the country's 70,000 public sector workers, who want higher wages and cuts in costs of transportation, fuel, electricity and water.
Reina on Thursday blasted the hospital workers' strike as "inhumane" and said a wage hike would be an unwise departure from the country's efforts to shore up its public finances.
Officials were upbeat on Thursday about reaching a settlement with the workers and have said the labour unrest does not represent a threat to political stability.
"We expect to reach an agreement this week and produce the first accords on the prices of public sector goods," Fernando Garcia, the Minister of Commerce and Industry, told reporters.
But the talks hit a snag when business leaders, who were also at the meeting, walked out and told the government they could not be asked to raise wages and also face higher costs for public services.
